scenarios.title: Light an LED safely
scenarios.objective: Understand why an LED needs a series resistor and what a switch does.

hints.LED_OVERCURRENT: Put the resistor in series between the battery and the LED so it limits the current.
hints.LED_REVERSED: An LED only conducts one way. Turn it around so the anode faces the battery's + side.
hints.NO_SOURCE: Every circuit needs a power source. Place the battery.
hints.MISSING_COMPONENT: This exercise uses a battery, a switch, a resistor, an LED and ground.
hints.WIRING_DIFFERS: All parts are there, but not in a single loop. Follow the current: battery, resistor, LED, ground, switch, back to the battery.

scenarios.title: Diode and buzzer
scenarios.objective: Understand a diode placed across a load and why its direction matters.

hints.SHORT_CIRCUIT: The diode is conducting straight across the battery. Flip it so it blocks current in normal operation.
hints.NO_SOURCE: Every circuit needs a power source. Place the battery.
hints.MISSING_COMPONENT: This exercise uses a battery, a switch, a diode, a buzzer and ground.
hints.WIRING_DIFFERS: The diode and the buzzer must be in parallel, after the switch.

scenarios.title: Distance display
scenarios.objective: Wire an ultrasonic sensor and an LCD to an Arduino and read a distance.

hints.SENSOR_NO_POWER: The sensor needs 5V and GND from the Arduino.
hints.LCD_NO_POWER: The LCD needs 5V on VDD and GND on VSS.
hints.WIRING_TRIG_ECHO: TRIG goes to D9 and ECHO to D10 (the pins used by the sketch).
hints.WIRING_LCD: Check RS to D12, E to D11 and D4 to D7 to D5 to D2.
hints.BACKLIGHT_NO_RESISTOR: The LCD backlight is an LED: put a resistor in series.
